verdict.rationale: First-party docs show push-based MFA approve/deny with number matching ("Tap or enter the corresponding number"). Admin control appears only indirectly: notifications are "allowed by your administrator", location sharing is required for country-restricted access, and a user reports his company enforces push-only Authenticator. Missing for 10: location context displayed in the push request, documented admin MFA policy configuration (e.g., enforcing number matching), independent corroboration of the number-matching phishing defense.

support.subject: As an IT admin, push-based sign-in includes phishing defenses — number matching, location context, and admin-enforced MFA policies

citations.quote: Tap or enter the corresponding number, then Approve.
Users can receive an MFA request on their mobile device, and approve or deny the sign-in attempt from their phone.
You'll need to share your location once every hour to ensure you're still within a country where you are allowed to access the resource.
You can set up notifications for your work or school account (if allowed by your administrator)
Now the only authenticator app my company allows is Microsoft Authenticator using push notifications.
